review_notes:
I read all 151 lines of the target file. I also read the definitions it depends on: `matrixTrace`, `matrixTracialState` and `matrixTraceLinear` in MatrixTraces.lean, `diagonalMatrixHom` and `diagonalMatrixHom_apply` in MatrixDiagonal.lean, and the `TracialState` structure. I followed downstream uses of `singleMatrix`, `scalarMatrixHom` and `TracialState.comap` in these files: FiniteFamilyMatrixCompletion, FiniteQuotientMatrixExtension, TwoQuasitraceBounds, QuasitraceMatrixDiagonal, FiniteSpectralTwoQuasitrace, FiniteFamilyMatrixTrace and MatrixSimplicity. I compared them with the Mathlib `Matrix.single` simp set: `single_mul_single_same`, `single_mul_single_of_ne`, `single_apply_same`/`single_apply_of_ne` and `conjTranspose_single` are all `@[simp]`. I also compared with the sibling `ComplexQuasitrace.comap_apply`, which is tagged `@[simp]`.

The file declares no simp lemmas at all. All four findings concern missing canonical simp/apply lemmas for its new definitions, which downstream code works around with `change`, by unfolding definitions, or by re-proving the same fact locally. I found no rewrite cycles or wrongly oriented simp lemmas. The `@[ext]` on `TracialState.ext` is appropriate.

Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemma proofs follow existing local proofs (for example the `change … conjTranspose …; rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_single]` pattern) but are untested. In particular, I have not checked that a fixed-`a` `scalarMatrixHom_apply` is accepted by `rfl` or by `simp`'s left-hand-side checks. The side condition of `singleMatrix_mul_ne` will only be discharged automatically by simp when the inequality is provable by simp or is in the simp set.

findings.excerpt:
lemma singleMatrix_mul_same (i j k : ι) (a b : A) :
    singleMatrix i j a * singleMatrix j k b = singleMatrix i k (a * b) := by
findings.problem: These are direct `CStarMatrix` versions of Mathlib's `Matrix.single_mul_single_same` and `Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne`, both of which are `@[simp]`. Here they are plain lemmas. As a result, every product of matrix units such as `singleMatrix i j a * singleMatrix j k b` has to be rewritten by name. This happens throughout the file (lines 67, 74) and downstream: `rw [hv, singleMatrix_mul_same]; simp [p]`, `simpa only [singleMatrix_mul_same, mul_one] using h`, and `rw [singleMatrix_mul_ne _ _ _ _ hjk, singleMatrix_mul_ne _ _ _ _ (Ne.symm hjk)]`. The `CStarMatrix.ofMatrix` wrapper means Mathlib's simp lemmas cannot fire on `singleMatrix` products.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `singleMatrix_mul_same` with `@[simp]`; its left-hand side is a product of two `singleMatrix` terms and its right-hand side is a single `singleMatrix`, so it cannot loop. Tag `singleMatrix_mul_ne` with `@[simp]` as well, with the hypothesis `hjk : j ≠ k` as a simp side condition, mirroring `Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne`. Optionally add a simp version of `Matrix.single_mul_mul_single` (`singleMatrix_sandwich` in MatrixSimplicity.lean is the special case `a = b = 1`).
findings.benefit: `simp` would normalise products of matrix units to a single unit or to `0`, just as it does for `Matrix.single`. Proofs like those in TwoQuasitraceBounds and QuasitraceMatrixDiagonal could then use plain `simp`/`simp [hjk]` instead of chains of named rewrites, and the simp set would match Mathlib's `Matrix.single` interface.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def singleMatrix (i j : ι) (a : A) : CStarMatrix ι ι A :=
  CStarMatrix.ofMatrix (Matrix.single i j a)
findings.problem: There is no lemma for `star (singleMatrix i j a)`. Its canonical form is `singleMatrix j i (star a)`, matching Mathlib's `@[simp] Matrix.conjTranspose_single`. Because `singleMatrix` hides the `ofMatrix`/`single` structure, simp cannot reach that Mathlib lemma. At least four downstream proofs re-prove the same fact locally with an identical `change … conjTranspose …; rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_single, …]` workaround (FiniteFamilyMatrixCompletion, FiniteQuotientMatrixExtension, TwoQuasitraceBounds twice, QuasitraceMatrixDiagonal).
findings.proposed_change:
Add next to the definition:
`@[simp] lemma star_singleMatrix (i j : ι) (a : A) : star (singleMatrix i j a) = singleMatrix j i (star a)`
Its proof can copy the local proofs: `change CStarMatrix.ofMatrix (Matrix.single i j a).conjTranspose = _; rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_single]; rfl`. The local `hs`/`hv` lemmas then become `by simp` (with `star_one`, which is already simp).
findings.benefit: This removes repeated ad hoc proofs. `simp` can then normalise expressions such as `star v * v` in polar-decomposition and orthogonality arguments (`cauchyMatrixLeg_orthogonal`, `finiteQuotientMatrixLeg_orthogonal`, `TwoQuasitrace.matrix_unit`) without unfolding the definition.

findings.excerpt: noncomputable def TracialState.comap (ρ : TracialState B) (φ : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) : TracialState A where
findings.problem: The pullback has no evaluation lemma, so `(ρ.comap φ).functional a` never simplifies to `ρ.functional (φ a)`. Every use has to go through definitional unfolding with `change`. Inside the definition: `change ρ.functional (φ a) ≤ …` and `change ρ.functional (φ 1) = 1`. In `matrixTrace_comap_scale`: `change (∑ i, ρ.functional (scalarMatrixHom (M i i))) = _`. By contrast, the analogous `ComplexQuasitrace.comap` in the same project has an `@[simp] comap_apply`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma TracialState.comap_functional_apply (ρ : TracialState B) (φ : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) (a : A) : (ρ.comap φ).functional a = ρ.functional (φ a) := rfl`. Then `matrixTrace_comap_scale` can begin with `simp only [matrixTrace_apply, TracialState.comap_functional_apply]` instead of the `change`.
findings.benefit: The left-to-right orientation removes the `comap` wrapper and moves toward the base functional. That is the canonical direction for pullbacks, and it cannot loop. Users of `ρ.comap scalarMatrixHom` (for example in the correspondence theorems at lines 104–140) could simplify evaluations without restating goals by hand, keeping the interface consistent with `ComplexQuasitrace.comap_apply`.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def scalarMatrixHom : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] CStarMatrix ι ι A where
  toFun a := diagonalMatrixHom (fun _ : ι => a)
findings.problem: `scalarMatrixHom` has no entry or coercion lemma, unlike `diagonalMatrixHom`, which has `@[simp] diagonalMatrixHom_apply`. As a result, `scalarMatrixHom a i j` is opaque to simp. In `comap_matrixTracialState` (lines 136–139) the goal must be restated with `change (∑ i : ι, τ.functional (diagonalMatrixHom (fun _ : ι => a) i i))` before `simp [diagonalMatrixHom_apply]` can run. That `simp` argument is itself redundant, since the lemma is already simp. Downstream, FiniteSpectralTwoQuasitrace unfolds the definitions wholesale with `simp [matrixSuccessor,scalarMatrixHom,diagonalMatrixHom,singleMatrix]` followed by `all_goals rfl`, which shows the missing entry lemmas for both `scalarMatrixHom` and `singleMatrix`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma scalarMatrixHom_apply (a : A) (i j : ι) : (scalarMatrixHom a : CStarMatrix ι ι A) i j = if i = j then a else 0 := rfl`, mirroring `diagonalMatrixHom_apply`. Add a matching `@[simp] lemma singleMatrix_apply (i j i' j' : ι) (a : A) : singleMatrix i j a i' j' = if i = i' ∧ j = j' then a else 0` (proved via `Matrix.single_apply`/`rfl`). Then the `change` at line 138 can go, and the proof becomes `simp [matrixTrace_apply]`. Downstream proofs can stop unfolding `scalarMatrixHom`, `diagonalMatrixHom` and `singleMatrix`.
findings.benefit: Entry-level simp lemmas are the canonical way to evaluate concrete matrices in ext-style proofs. With them, `CStarMatrix.ext; simp` works on goals involving these new definitions without exposing their internal construction. This makes proofs such as `firstMatrixCorner_eq_single` and `TwoQuasitrace.matrix_unit` (`simp [p, q, singleMatrix, Matrix.single]`) robust to changes in how the definitions are implemented.
